stories.headline: US envoys arrive in Moscow ahead of Ukraine talks
stories.summary: US diplomatic representatives have arrived in Moscow to pursue negotiations aimed at resolving the Ukraine conflict, signaling a renewed diplomatic effort between the two countries. Russia has announced a temporary pause in military strikes during the talks, though recent attacks on Ukrainian targets including intelligence facilities underscore the ongoing violence underlying these negotiations.

stories.headline: How big is Africa really? Why the UN voted to change the world map
stories.summary: The United Nations has adopted a new world map that displays Africa at its true geographic size, correcting a centuries-old cartographic distortion caused by the Mercator projection. The change addresses how traditional maps have systematically enlarged northern continents while shrinking Africa, a visual representation that has influenced global perceptions of relative importance and power.

stories.headline: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flood disaster
stories.summary: Search and rescue teams in Nepal have located two additional survivors from the recent flooding, bringing hope to ongoing recovery efforts more than a week after the disaster struck. The death toll has climbed to 1,344, with hundreds more missing across the region, including 275 Indian nationals unaccounted for.

stories.headline: Lindsay Clancy murder trial has divided US on whether she's victim or criminal
stories.summary: A mistrial has been declared in the case of Lindsay Clancy, who was charged with killing her three young children in Massachusetts in 2022, after jurors could not reach a unanimous verdict. The case has sparked broad public debate about whether Clancy should be viewed primarily as a woman suffering from severe mental illness or as a criminal responsible for her actions.

stories.headline: Israel must protect West Bank’s Palestinians amid settler pogroms: US envoy
stories.summary: A U.S. envoy is calling on Israel to enforce protection for Palestinians in the West Bank as violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinian communities continues to escalate. The ambassador's statements follow recent incidents in which Palestinian teenagers were killed and settlers have surrounded villages, prompting demands for stronger Israeli enforcement action and consequences for the perpetrators.

stories.headline: Bolivian military barracks explosion kills at least 10
stories.summary: An explosion at a Bolivian military barracks in Viacha has killed at least 10 people, with dozens more injured and some still missing following the blast. Authorities have not yet identified the cause of the explosion, though investigations are underway.

stories.headline: Germany's far-right AfD bids for first taste of power in eastern vote
stories.summary: The AfD, Germany's far-right party, is competing in the Saxony-Anhalt state election where it could enter a regional government for the first time if smaller parties prove willing to form a coalition with it. Traditional parties have largely refused to work with the AfD, making any power-sharing arrangement dependent on negotiations with minor political players.

stories.headline: At least four civilians killed in Houthi missile strike near Yemen’s Taiz
stories.summary: A Houthi missile strike near Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, has killed at least four civilians as fighting escalates across the country's western regions. The attack occurs amid intensified clashes that have claimed over 120 lives, marking some of the deadliest combat Yemen has experienced in recent years.

stories.headline: Iran war: Explosions reported near Kharg Island
stories.summary: A U.S. missile strike on an Iranian oil tanker near Kharg Island, a major petroleum export hub in the Persian Gulf, has triggered explosions in the region. The incident escalates tensions between the two nations and raises concerns about disruptions to global oil supplies from one of the world's critical energy chokepoints.

stories.headline: Germany, partners aim to finalize 'return hubs' by year end
stories.summary: Germany and four partner nations are establishing external processing centers where rejected asylum applicants will be held while deportation procedures are completed. The countries aim to finalize these "return hubs" in non-EU locations by the end of this year, with full operational capacity expected by 2027.
